__line_text__: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease primarily caused by

label: body
__line_text__: inhibition of cartilage extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis and promotion of

label: body
__line_text__: cartilage is tissue destruction. Many etiological risk factors and

label: body
__line_text__: pathophysiological processes associated with aging contribute to the

label: body
__line_text__: progression of osteoarthritis. Joint instability, mechanical stress including

label: body
__line_text__: injury, and aging-related factors that predispose one to osteoarthritis are

label: body
__line_text__: potential osteoarthritis-causing mechanisms. These factors activate

label: body
__line_text__: biochemical pathways in chondrocytes which are a unique cell type that

label: body
__line_text__: synthesizes various catabolic and anabolic factors, leading to degradation of

label: body
__line_text__: the ECM by matrix metalloproteinase (Mmp) and cessation of ECM synthesis via

label: body
__line_text__: dedifferentiation and apoptosis of chondrocytes (Pelletier J P et al.,

label: metadata
__line_text__: Arthritis Rheum., 44:1237-47, 2001). In particular, cartilage tissue that

label: body
__line_text__: constitutes a joint is not normally regenerated in vivo once it is damaged. If

label: body
__line_text__: cartilage tissue in a joint is damaged, the cartilage tissue damage impedes

label: body
__line_text__: daily activities with severe pain. If the damage becomes chronic, it causes

label: body
__line_text__: fatal osteoarthritis which interferes with normal life or professional

label: body
__line_text__: activities.

label: body
__line_text__: Until now, therapeutic agents for arthritis have not been developed.

label: body
__line_text__: Generally, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are used for the

label: body
__line_text__: purpose of alleviating joint inflammation. However, since NSAID-based drugs

label: body
__line_text__: are primarily intended to temporarily relieve joint inflammation, NSAID-based

label: body
__line_text__: drugs do not provide adequate treatment for osteoarthritis which is a non-

label: body
__line_text__: inflammatory arthritis that requires enhancement of cartilage formation and

label: body
__line_text__: inhibition of cartilage destruction (Pritchard M H et al., Annals of the

label: metadata
__line_text__: Rheumatic Diseases, 37:493-503, 1978). Such NSAIDs are suitable as a

label: body
__line_text__: therapeutic agent for the prevention of inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis

label: body
__line_text__: which is an inflammatory arthritis. However, it is pointed out that NSAIDs

label: body
__line_text__: accelerate cartilage damage or have adverse effects on the cardiovascular

label: body
__line_text__: system, gastrointestinal tract, kidney, liver, etc.
